meta.title: Security & Trust
meta.description: How MCPEmails protects your email: fetched live and never stored, credentials encrypted at rest, scoped and revocable access, and public code you can read or self-host.

hero.title: You shouldn't have to take my word for it
hero.lead: MCPEmails connects an AI agent to your inbox, so it has to earn real trust. This is the honest version: what the service touches, what it keeps, what it can never do, and how you can verify all of it yourself.

tldr.title: 1. The short version
tldr.intro: If you read nothing else on this page:
points: Your email is fetched live on each request and dropped the moment the response is sent. We keep no copy of any message body, subject, attachment, or contact.
We store exactly one sensitive thing per inbox: an access token or app password, encrypted with AES-256-GCM, so we can make the next call you ask for.
We never train any AI model on your email, and we never send your email to a model of our own choosing. Your agent is the only thing that reads it, under your control.
Every connection is scoped to the single inbox you connected, and you can revoke it at any time from Google, Microsoft, or your provider's settings.
The code that runs the service is public. You can read it, audit it, or self-host the whole thing.

access.title: 2. What we access vs. what we store
access.intro: The gap between access and storage is the whole design. In the moment, the agent can read a lot, live. Almost none of it is ever written down.

rows.accessed: Live, only when your agent makes a read or search call
rows.stored: Never written to disk, cache, or logs

rows.accessed: Scanned live from recent mail when asked
rows.stored: Never. There is no stored address book

rows.accessed: Decrypted only inside an isolated function at call time
rows.stored: Yes, encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM; key held separately

rows.accessed: Compared as a hash on every request
rows.stored: Only a SHA-256 hash; the raw key is shown once and is never recoverable

rows.accessed: Held until the send time, then dispatched
rows.stored: Yes, encrypted at rest until sent, then kept as your history

rows.accessed: Recorded for your own audit log
rows.stored: Tool name, inbox, timestamp, and status only. No email content

access.outro: The one deliberate exception is a message you ask the agent to schedule for later. We have to hold it until the send time, so we store it encrypted in the meantime, then keep a record afterwards for your history.

verify.title: 3. You don't have to trust me, you can check
verify.p1: "A random person vibe-coded this" is a fair worry for any hosted tool that touches your email. The right answer is not a bigger promise. It is removing the need to take me at my word.
points: Read the code. The server that runs MCPEmails is public on GitHub. You can see exactly what it keeps (an encrypted token) and what it doesn't (your mail).
Self-host it. If you would rather not use the hosted service at all, you can run the same code on your own infrastructure with your own keys.
Use a scoped, revocable connection. You connect with OAuth or an app password that grants only mail access, and you can revoke it in one click from your provider, with no involvement from me.
Watch what it does. Every tool call your agent makes is recorded in an activity log you can read, so you can see precisely what was accessed and when.
verify.outro: And if a native connector already covers your provider and does what you need, use it. This exists for the providers and multi-inbox combinations they don't cover.

injection.title: 4. The real risk: prompt injection
injection.p1: The honest threat here is not me reading your mail. It is a hostile email trying to hijack the agent: instructions hidden inside a message that try to make your AI forward, delete, or leak something. This is a real, unsolved problem for every email agent. I won't claim it's solved. I can show how it's contained:
points: One inbox, one token. A connection can only ever touch the single inbox you connected it to. A scoped token cannot reach your other inboxes, or anyone else's.
Destructive actions are separated and flagged. Sending and deleting are their own tools, marked destructive, so your AI client asks for confirmation before they fire.
Least privilege. Connections request mail read and compose access, not account-wide control. Even a fully compromised token is bounded by the scope you granted.
Rate limited. Every key is rate limited, so a runaway or hijacked agent cannot fan out thousands of actions unnoticed.
injection.outro: Not solved. Contained: the irreversible actions are gated, and the blast radius is kept to one inbox.

credentials.title: 5. How your credentials are protected
credentials.intro: Your tokens are the only sensitive thing we hold, so they get the strongest protection we can give them:
measures: All data in transit is encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher. Connections that do not support TLS are rejected.
OAuth tokens and IMAP credentials are encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM. The encryption key is held separately from the encrypted data and is never co-located with it.
API keys are hashed with SHA-256 before storage. The raw key cannot be recovered from the hash.
Database access is protected by Row-Level Security policies that stop one workspace from reaching another's data, even if a query is written wrong.
Administrative access to production infrastructure requires multi-factor authentication and is logged.

google.title: 6. Google and provider verification
google.p1: Gmail access uses Google's restricted scopes, the tier Google scrutinises most closely. We are completing Google's restricted-scope OAuth verification and its annual CASA security assessment, carried out by an independent, Google-approved assessor. Once it is complete, you will no longer see Google's "unverified app" warning when you connect.
google.p2: MCPEmails' use and transfer of information received from Google APIs to any other app adheres to the <link>Google API Services User Data Policy</link>, including the Limited Use requirements.
google.p3: For Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, and other IMAP providers, you connect with a provider-issued app password that you can revoke at any time, with no broad OAuth scopes for us to over-request.

subprocessors.title: 7. Subprocessors
subprocessors.intro: We keep the list of companies that touch any data short, and each is bound by a data processing agreement. Note what is absent: no AI provider is on this list. MCPEmails does not send your email to any model of its own. Your agent does that, under your control and its provider's data policy.

rows.location: EU (Frankfurt) or US (Virginia); you choose at signup
Global edge, nearest region to user

rows.purpose: Payment processing (billing only, no email data)

report.title: 8. Reporting a vulnerability
report.p1: If you find a security issue, please report it. I would much rather hear it from you than read about it later.
points: Email <securityEmail></securityEmail> with details and steps to reproduce.
A machine-readable contact is published at <securitytxt>/.well-known/security.txt</securitytxt>.
I aim to acknowledge reports within 24 hours and to fix confirmed critical issues within 72 hours.
report.safeHarbor: Safe harbour. If you make a good-faith effort to follow this policy, do not access or modify other users' data, and give me a reasonable chance to fix the issue before disclosing it, I will not pursue or support legal action against you for your research.

cta.title: Questions about any of this?
cta.sub: Ask me anything. I'm the only person running this, and I answer every message.
